payer: the holder of a Binance dated (quarterly) futures contract, force-delivered at a published index average on a calendar minute
why_they_keep_paying: Delivery price is a mechanical per-second average of the index over a fixed clock window before 08:00 UTC on the last Friday of the quarter (07:00-08:00 for the whole 2019-2024 period; shortened to 07:30-08:00 only on 2024-11-11), and the contract goes Reduce-Only 10 minutes before delivery, so the holder can neither choose an exit price nor re-open. Anyone who wants the exposure to continue past expiry must roll on the exchange's calendar rather than their own.
what_would_end_it: Retirement of dated contracts in favour of continuously rolling ones, or a settlement defined on a price the holder can actually transact against (a closing auction) instead of a backward-looking average during a window in which they are locked out.
observable: In 1-minute perpetual bars, the 07:00-08:00 UTC hour of the last Friday of March, June, September and December should differ from the same hour on ordinary Fridays and on the last Friday of non-quarter months - in intrabar range, in signed drift across the hour, and in what happens to that move after 08:00. The footprint should exist only for the assets that actually had a listed dated contract (BTC, ETH), leaving the several hundred alt perps as a within-venue, same-minute control.
needs_data_we_lack: prices and open interest of the dated quarterly contracts themselves; the Binance index price series used for settlement; off-venue option expiry open interest, which shares the same 08:00 UTC fixing convention and would be needed to attribute the flow rather than merely detect it
distinct_from: The payment is a fixing on a calendar the exchange publishes and is owed by any holder of a dated contract irrespective of side or leverage, whereas every closed family is paid per 8-hour settlement by whoever stands on the crowded side of a perpetual.

payer: the holder of a large position in a named symbol whose margin tiers Binance has announced it will tighten at a stated timestamp
why_they_keep_paying: Binance unilaterally rewrites the notional-to-maintenance-margin ladder for individual symbols with a few days' notice and states plainly that existing positions are affected and must be reduced before the effective minute or face liquidation - MTLUSDT's top tier, for example, was moved so that 1x and 50% maintenance margin began at 4m instead of 6m USDT. The ladder exists to cap the exchange's own tail risk, so it keeps being tightened precisely in the symbols whose inventory is hardest to exit.
what_would_end_it: Grandfathering positions opened under the old ladder, or cross-symbol portfolio margining that stops the constraint from binding symbol by symbol.
observable: In the affected symbol alone, the minutes before the announced effective timestamp should carry one-sided forced reduction - abnormal volume and abnormal range against whichever side is large - with neighbouring symbols and the same clock time on adjacent days as controls. Nothing should show up in that symbol's funding history, because the payment is not a funding settlement; that absence is itself the discriminator.
needs_data_we_lack: the archive of Binance leverage- and margin-tier change announcements with their effective timestamps, and the historical per-symbol margin-tier tables. Neither is in the 1-minute panel, the funding history or the listing/delisting table; both would have to be collected from the exchange's announcement pages before the mechanism could be measured at all.
distinct_from: This is a scheduled, pre-announced deleveraging forced by a rulebook change rather than by price, so the payer is identified by position size in one named symbol at one announced minute - not by being the crowded funding-payer, and not by being margin-called in a cascade.

payer: the trader whose futures collateral is a private stablecoin that the venue values at exactly 1.0000 USD and who holds no par-redemption right of their own
why_they_keep_paying: Margin, PnL and liquidation on a USDⓈ-M contract are all computed in the quote stablecoin at a hard one-dollar peg, while the actual 1:1 redemption right sits only with onboarded customers of the issuer - Paxos guaranteed BUSD redemption to onboarded customers through at least February 2024, and Binance later force-converted leftover BUSD futures balances to USDT on its own timetable starting 2023-12-14. The venue offers no dollar rail, so the marginal trader cannot opt out of holding issuer credit as the unit of account.
what_would_end_it: Collateral marked at its traded price rather than at par, native USD or tokenised-treasury margin, or an on-venue redemption facility open to every holder rather than to onboarded issuer clients.
observable: This venue ran perps on the same asset quoted in different stablecoins side by side - BTCUSDT against BTCBUSD, ETHUSDT against ETHBUSD, and later USDC-quoted pairs. If the mechanism is real, the same-minute price ratio between such a pair steps within a single minute during peg stress and around the announced wind-down dates, and - unlike a funding differential, which drifts smoothly - that step is simultaneous and same-signed across every symbol sharing the quote asset, which is a cross-sectional signature no per-symbol basis can imitate.
needs_data_we_lack: confirmation that 1-minute bars for the BUSD-quoted and USDC-quoted USDⓈ-M perps are actually in the archive (the BUSD contracts were settled and delisted 2023-12-08 and 2023-12-11 and may simply be absent), plus an off-venue stablecoin/USD price such as USDT/USD or BUSD/USD spot elsewhere, without which one can only say the two legs diverged and not which leg moved
distinct_from: The payment is on the collateral's unit of account and is owed by longs and shorts alike, including a perfectly delta-hedged book with no directional exposure at all, whereas every closed family requires a directional perpetual position and is paid through the funding settlement.

payer: the holder of an open position in a perp Binance has announced it will retire, and the spot-versus-perp hedger who loses their only shortable leg on the exchange's date
why_they_keep_paying: Binance routinely retires low-liquidity contracts on roughly a week's notice, suspends trading and switches to reduce-only shortly before the cutoff, then closes every remaining position by automatic settlement at an index average the holder cannot transact against - the exchange states that its settlement-price rule covers delisting-subject contracts as well as delivery contracts. For many of these tokens the perp was the only venue where the exposure could be shorted at all, so a hedged holder must unwind the entire structure on a date the venue chose.
what_would_end_it: Longer notice, positions made transferable into a replacement contract, or settlement referenced to a deep spot venue instead of a thin index on a dying token.
observable: The project already holds the listing/delisting table, so the final sessions of the delisted symbols can be aligned on their own clock rather than on wall-clock time: 1-minute bars should show volume collapsing while intrabar range widens, a signed drift through the last hours, and a discontinuity at the announced settlement hour that symbols still listed on those same dates never display.
needs_data_we_lack: the announcement (notice) date and the exact settlement timestamp for each historical delisting - the held table records the delisting date, not when the venue told anyone - plus the index price used at settlement. KT-3 already found that only 481 of 986 symbols ever traded have bars locally and 266 are delisted, so the honest risk is that the aligned ensemble is too small to support any statement, and that should be checked before anything is registered.
distinct_from: The constraint here is the venue withdrawing the instrument itself on a published date, which extracts payment from both legs of a hedge and from shorts as readily as longs, so it depends on neither crowding nor leverage nor the funding rate; it is also not a basket claim - each delisting is its own dated event, though the sample of such events is exactly what KT-3 says is thin.

payer: a leveraged Binance USD-M perpetual short whose collateral has fallen below maintenance margin
why_they_keep_paying: Binance removes the trader's discretion and submits an Immediate-or-Cancel order to buy back the short, while also charging a liquidation-clearance fee. The constraint is the exchange's maintenance-margin and liquidation protocol, not a voluntary reaction to price.
what_would_end_it: The forced payment would stop if the position were closed or recapitalized before breaching maintenance margin, or if Binance replaced market liquidation with a mechanism that did not execute the position against the market.
observable: If forced short covering has a material footprint, sharp upward one-minute moves should exhibit asymmetric continuation and elevated volume, followed by relaxation once the compulsory buy flow is exhausted.
needs_data_we_lack: Binance liquidation-order records or forced-order stream, mark-price bars, account leverage and collateral, and open interest are needed to distinguish forced short covering from ordinary aggressive buying.
distinct_from: The payer is a liquidated short forced to buy into an upward move, not a funding-paying leveraged long or a liquidated long selling into a cascade.

payer: a short-gamma BTC or ETH options dealer executing compulsory delta rebalancing through Binance USD-M perpetuals
why_they_keep_paying: The dealer's outstanding option liability and delta-risk limit require buying as the underlying rises and selling as it falls, especially as gamma concentrates near expiry. This flow persists because abandoning the hedge would violate the dealer's inventory-risk constraint.
what_would_end_it: The pressure ends when the options expire or are closed, the dealer's net gamma becomes non-negative, or the hedge is moved away from Binance perpetuals.
observable: Binance BTCUSDT or ETHUSDT one-minute bars could show increased volume and same-direction price acceleration during the 07:30-08:00 UTC Deribit expiry window, followed by reversal after the expiring exposure and its hedge disappear.
needs_data_we_lack: Options open interest by strike and expiry, dealer-position or gamma estimates, and venue-level hedge-flow data are required to identify the sign and magnitude of the compulsory hedge rather than merely testing a calendar footprint.
distinct_from: The payer is an options intermediary constrained by nonlinear inventory exposure, and the payment is adverse hedge execution rather than perpetual funding or long-side liquidation.
